text:
jamie_ops: quick note — i'm taking the 22:00->02:00 latechange swap tonight. i'll be PRIMARY, @priya_oncall you'll be SECONDARY unless you want to swap? :wave:

priya_oncall: i can stay secondary, thanks. what's the current risk surface?

jamie_ops: short summary: after the 18:30 deploy we started seeing intermittent kv-cache write timeouts hitting payment-queue path. customer-facing symptom = delayed receipts & sporadic duplicate events. impact ~2-3% of requests in the last hour.

incident_bot: Pager triggered: KV_CACHE_WRITE_ERRORS > 0.05 over 5m for service=payment-queue (alert #4932).

matt_infra: chiming in — i've seen the same in traces. appears to be a timeout spike on the write path to the new quantized cache nodes. fallback to redis-fallback is functioning but at reduced throughput.

ana_support: ops ticket opened with affected customer ids sample attached: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INC-4932 (sensitive). priority P1 for impacting receipts.

jamie_ops: priority checklist below — follow these in order and call me if anything blocks. paste into thread so secondary has the list.

jamie_ops: 1) Confirm current primary/secondary: PRIMARY=jamie_ops, SECONDARY=priya_oncall. if both green, proceed with investigation steps.

jamie_ops: 2) Quick mitigation: enable write-fanout to legacy redis fallback (already partially on). run:
```
# on prod control plane
redwoodctl feature toggle set payment_kv_write_fanout=true --env=prod
```
Expectation: reduces write timeout errors within 30s.

priya_oncall: running the toggle now. will post logs. :eyes:

incident_bot: Action logged: feature toggle set by priya_oncall at 1923456798.

matt_infra: 3) If toggle not reducing errors, scale up cache nodes 2x:
```
kubectl -n inference scale rs/kv-cache-quant --replicas=6
```
Fallback: route traffic to region-b with `traffic-shift payment-queue --to region-b --pct 30`

jamie_ops: 4) Diagnostics quick queries:
`kubectl logs -l app=kv-cache -n prod --tail=200 | grep WARN
`
`traces view --service payment-queue --filter "error && kv_write" --last 15m`

ana_support: Customer comms note (draft): "We're investigating reduced write performance affecting a small subset of receipts. We're rolling back mitigating changes and will update within 30 minutes." use at-will.

priya_oncall: toggle applied. error-rate dropping from 0.08 -> 0.02 in the last 90s. still watching. :thumbsup:

jamie_ops: great — keep watching for 5m. if it bounces back over 0.05, escalate to on-call lead (matt_infra) and prepare rollback of 18:30 deploy: `deploy rollback --to 2026-03-14-18:00`

matt_infra: i'll be available if escalated. also putting runbook links here for quick access:
- KV cache runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-write-failures
- Traffic shift playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/traffic-shift
- Customer comms templates: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/customer-comms

jamie_ops: note on postmortem: capture the sequence: deploy->quantized nodes->timeouts->fallback fanout. tag evals team for possible regression in quantized write path.

priya_oncall: still stable at 0.02 after 7m. i'll keep secondary watch until 02:00 and will handover to morningsync if needed.

ana_support: i've queued a proactive message to the affected list and linked the draft.

jamie_ops: perfect. handover plan for tomorrow: i'll add a short Handoff message to #eng-oncall at 01:50 with status + any open remediation tickets. if anything degrades, page both primary & secondary.

sre-bot: Reminder: when marking incident resolved, include metric windows and the toggle roll history for audit.

priya_oncall: acknowledged. ping me at any time. leaving a note in my calendar.

jamie_ops: thanks team. keeping this thread live for updates. if anyone joins later — read the first message for the primary/secondary assignment and follow the checklist. :white_check_mark:
